newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Iberdrola to raise Tractebel stake -paper.
newsitem.headline: Iberdrola to raise Tractebel stake -paper.

text.p: Spanish utility Iberdrola plans to raise its stake in Belgian utility holding company Tractebel to five percent, Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said on Friday.
The paper said Iberdrola, which currently has 0.5 percent of Tractebel, now had sufficient cash to carry out the plan as stated in a letter of intent signed in 1991.
The paper said that Spanish financiers viewed the stake in Tractebel as a logical continuation of the internationalisation and diversification process at Iberdrola.
The FET said the news came in an article in Spanish magazine Expansion.

Tractebel, 65 percent owned by Belgium's flagship holding company Societe Generale de Belgique, already holds five percent in Iberdrola. The paper said the Spanish group, which with Tractebel already is in a number of joint projects, might buy shares on the bourse or take a stake in Tractebel's Electrabel.
Through its control of Electrabel, Tractebel has a virtual monopoly in energy production in Belgium.
A direct stake in Electrabel would give Iberdrola an indirect influence in Tractebel.
Tractebel's other main arm is Powerfin, a company set up to spearhead Tractebel's expansion drive in the electricy sector abroad.

Tractebel plans to merge the two companies to simplfy group structure, but this is expected to involve an issue of new stock which would cut SGB's stake in Tractebel to 53 percent, reducing SGB's willingness to sell shares to Iberdrola, the FET said.

The paper said that in view of the planned merger, the stated intention by SGB owners to hold at least 50 percent in Tractebel via SGB while encouraging fresh Flemish participation in the company, there was little chance of SGB selling part of its holding to Iberdrola.
SGB is 63 percent owned by French holding company Cie de Suez.
On the Brussels bourse Tractbel shares were up 25 francs at 14,650 at 0950 GMT.
